title: Playing a game
text: rk_world() returns classic 42-territory board rk_map. Plotting map alone shows adjacency graph coloured continent. Note Alaska Kamchatka: board wraps around, segment crosses whole picture.  Custom boards welcome; rk_map() validates graph (must symmetric, every territory must belong exactly one continent) lays board give circle supply coordinates.
code: world <- rk_world() world #> <rk_map> 42 territories, 6 continents #> Bonuses: North_America +5, South_America +2, Europe +5, Africa +3, Asia +7, and Australia +2 world$continent_bonus #> North_America South_America        Europe        Africa          Asia  #>             5             2             5             3             7  #>     Australia  #>             2 rk_neighbors(world, "Brazil") #> [1] "Venezuela"    "Peru"         "Argentina"    "North_Africa" rk_plot_map(world) mini <- rk_map(   territories = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),   adjacency = list(     A = c("B", "C"), B = c("A", "D"), C = c("A", "D"), D = c("B", "C")   ),   continent = list(North = c("A", "B"), South = c("C", "D")),   continent_bonus = c(North = 2, South = 3) ) mini #> <rk_map> 4 territories, 2 continents #> Bonuses: North +2 and South +3

text: turn runs three phases. Every function returns new game, can keep old one compare, replay branch.

title: Playing a game
text: allowance one army per three territories, never fewer three, plus bonus every continent held outright. Placements named vector must account every army:
code: rk_reinforcements(game, "Red") #> [1] 4 front <- rk_legal_attacks(game, "Red") head(front, 3) #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   from                to      defender att_armies def_armies #>   <chr>               <chr>   <chr>         <int>      <int> #> 1 Northwest_Territory Alaska  Blue              3          2 #> 2 Northwest_Territory Alberta Blue              3          3 #> 3 Northwest_Territory Ontario Green             3          3  placements <- c(rk_reinforcements(game, "Red")) names(placements) <- front$from[[1]] game <- rk_reinforce(game, "Red", placements) game$phase #> [1] "attack"

title: Playing a game
text: attack resolved rk_battle() internally, odds apply combat engine — rk_battle_odds() tell beforehand getting :
code: set.seed(7) targets <- rk_legal_attacks(game, "Red") best <- targets[which.min(targets$def_armies), ] best #> # A tibble: 1 × 5 #>   from  to        defender att_armies def_armies #>   <chr> <chr>     <chr>         <int>      <int> #> 1 Peru  Argentina Green             2          1  game <- rk_attack(game, best$from, best$to) game$last_battle #> <rk_battle> territory repelled after 1 duel #> Attacker: 1 left · Defender: 1 left rk_owner(game, best$to) #> [1] "Green" rk_battle_odds(best$att_armies, best$def_armies, method = "exact") #> # A tibble: 1 × 7 #>   att_armies def_armies method     n p_conquer e_att_survivors e_def_survivors #>        <int>      <int> <chr>  <int>     <dbl>           <dbl>           <dbl> #> 1          2          1 exact     NA     0.417            1.42           0.583

title: Playing a game
text: One move along path territories ends turn.
code: own <- rk_territories(game, "Red") from <- own[which.max(rk_armies(game, own))] reachable <- intersect(rk_neighbors(game, from), own) if (length(reachable) > 0 && rk_armies(game, from) > 1) {   game <- rk_fortify(game, from, reachable[[1]], 1) } game <- rk_end_turn(game) game$turn #> [1] "Blue"

title: Playing a game
text: rk_ai() returns policy — function (game, player) proposes action. rk_step() applies one action; rk_play() runs whole game. result carries standings every round, makes shape game easy see:
code: bot <- rk_ai("aggressive") bot(game, game$turn)$action #> [1] "reinforce" set.seed(11) result <- rk_play(   game,   policies = c(Red = "aggressive", Blue = "cautious", Green = "random"),   max_rounds = 40 ) result #> <rk_game_result> 3 players #> Winner: Blue after 18 rounds #> Policies: Red (aggressive), Blue (cautious), and Green (random) standings <- result$standings ggplot2::ggplot(   standings,   ggplot2::aes(round, territories, colour = player) ) +   ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +   ggplot2::labs(     x = "round", y = "territories held", colour = NULL,     title = "Who was winning, and when"   ) +   ggplot2::theme_minimal() rk_plot_map(result$game)

title: Playing a game
text: policy function (game, player) returns action list, new strategy lines. one always reinforces weakest territory never attacks: Turtling work. Neither anything else, reliably — rk_tournament() exists.
code: turtle <- function(game, player) {   if (identical(game$phase, "reinforce")) {     own <- rk_territories(game, player)     placements <- rk_reinforcements(game, player)     names(placements) <- own[which.min(rk_armies(game, own))]     return(list(action = "reinforce", placements = placements))   }   list(action = "end_turn") }  set.seed(5) turtle_result <- rk_play(   rk_game(c("Red", "Blue"), seed = 5),   policies = list(Red = rk_ai("aggressive"), Blue = turtle),   max_rounds = 25 ) turtle_result #> <rk_game_result> 2 players #> Winner: Red after 8 rounds #> Policies: Red (custom) and Blue (custom)

title: Getting started with risikoR
text: heart Risk dice duel. attacker rolls three dice, defender two, highest dice compared pairwise. attacker must roll strictly higher: ties go defender. rk_duel_dist() enumerates 6^3 * 6^2 = 7776 equally likely combinations, probabilities exact rather simulated: rk_duel_odds() summarises enumeration: attacker expects lose 0.92 armies defender 1.08 per three--two duel — standard textbook values.
code: set.seed(1) rk_duel(3, 2) #> $att_loss #> [1] 2 #>  #> $def_loss #> [1] 0 #>  #> $att_roll #> [1] 4 1 1 #>  #> $def_roll #> [1] 5 2 rk_duel_dist(3, 2) #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   n_att n_def att_loss def_loss     p #>   <int> <int>    <int>    <int> <dbl> #> 1     3     2        0        2 0.372 #> 2     3     2        1        1 0.336 #> 3     3     2        2        0 0.293 rk_duel_odds(3, 2) #> # A tibble: 1 × 8 #>   n_att n_def e_att_loss e_def_loss sd_loss p_att_wins_all p_def_wins_all #>   <int> <int>      <dbl>      <dbl>   <dbl>          <dbl>          <dbl> #> 1     3     2      0.921       1.08   0.811          0.372          0.293 #> # ℹ 1 more variable: p_split <dbl> rk_plot_duel(3, 2)

title: Getting started with risikoR
text: rk_battle_odds() answers question actually matters table: attack succeed? "exact" method solves underlying Markov chain, simulation error involved; "mc" simulates instead. Ten attackers beat five defenders four times five; ten fifteen almost never win:
code: rk_battle_odds(20, 15, method = "exact") #> # A tibble: 1 × 7 #>   att_armies def_armies method     n p_conquer e_att_survivors e_def_survivors #>        <int>      <int> <chr>  <int>     <dbl>           <dbl>           <dbl> #> 1         20         15 exact     NA     0.822            7.83           0.719  set.seed(1) rk_battle_odds(20, 15, n = 1000) #> # A tibble: 1 × 7 #>   att_armies def_armies method     n p_conquer e_att_survivors e_def_survivors #>        <int>      <int> <chr>  <int>     <dbl>           <dbl>           <dbl> #> 1         20         15 mc      1000     0.827            8.02           0.682 rk_odds_table(att_range = c(10, 20), def_range = c(5, 15)) #> # A tibble: 4 × 6 #>   att_armies def_armies method p_conquer e_att_survivors e_def_survivors #>        <int>      <int> <chr>      <dbl>           <dbl>           <dbl> #> 1         10          5 exact      0.873            6.07         0.305   #> 2         10         15 exact      0.173            1.61         6.02    #> 3         20          5 exact      0.999           16.0          0.00294 #> 4         20         15 exact      0.822            7.83         0.719

title: The probability of Risk
text: 6^n_att * 6^n_def equally likely combinations, enough enumerate exhaustively. rk_duel_dist() exactly . Three attacking dice two defending dice standard case, worth memorising: attacker loses nothing 37% time, trades one one 34% time, loses two 29% time. Comparing every legal dice pairing shows much extra dice worth: Two lessons fall . Rolling three dice instead one roughly halves attacker’s expected loss, never attack fewer armies need three dice. defender’s second die worth attacker’s third: two defending dice attacker loses armies defender every pairing.
code: rk_duel_dist(3, 2) #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   n_att n_def att_loss def_loss     p #>   <int> <int>    <int>    <int> <dbl> #> 1     3     2        0        2 0.372 #> 2     3     2        1        1 0.336 #> 3     3     2        2        0 0.293 pairings <- expand.grid(n_att = 1:3, n_def = 1:2) odds <- do.call(   rbind,   Map(rk_duel_odds, pairings$n_att, pairings$n_def) ) odds[order(odds$n_def, odds$n_att), ] #> # A tibble: 6 × 8 #>   n_att n_def e_att_loss e_def_loss sd_loss p_att_wins_all p_def_wins_all #>   <int> <int>      <dbl>      <dbl>   <dbl>          <dbl>          <dbl> #> 1     1     1      0.583      0.417   0.493          0.417          0.583 #> 2     2     1      0.421      0.579   0.494          0.579          0.421 #> 3     3     1      0.340      0.660   0.474          0.660          0.340 #> 4     1     2      0.745      0.255   0.436          0.255          0.745 #> 5     2     2      1.22       0.779   0.792          0.228          0.448 #> 6     3     2      0.921      1.08    0.811          0.372          0.293 #> # ℹ 1 more variable: p_split <dbl>

title: The probability of Risk
text: battle repeats duel one side runs . duel removes fixed number armies, process absorbing Markov chain states (attacker armies, defender armies) — rk_battle_odds(method = "exact") solves directly. Monte Carlo estimate converges : Holding attacker fixed varying defender traces conquest curve:  crossing point number remember: attacker needs roughly 5--4 advantage even odds, 3--2 advantage comfortable. whole surface :
code: rk_battle_odds(10, 8, method = "exact") #> # A tibble: 1 × 7 #>   att_armies def_armies method     n p_conquer e_att_survivors e_def_survivors #>        <int>      <int> <chr>  <int>     <dbl>           <dbl>           <dbl> #> 1         10          8 exact     NA     0.646            4.05            1.23 set.seed(1) mc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(   c(100, 1000, 10000),   function(n) rk_battle_odds(10, 8, n = n) )) mc$exact <- rk_battle_odds(10, 8, method = "exact")$p_conquer mc[, c("n", "p_conquer", "exact")] #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>       n p_conquer exact #>   <int>     <dbl> <dbl> #> 1   100     0.56  0.646 #> 2  1000     0.642 0.646 #> 3 10000     0.651 0.646 rk_plot_conquest(20, def_range = 1:25, method = "exact") odds_grid <- rk_odds_table(att_range = 2:20, def_range = 1:20) even <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(odds_grid, odds_grid$def_armies), function(d) {   win <- d[d$p_conquer >= 0.5, ]   if (nrow(win) == 0) return(NULL)   win[1, c("def_armies", "att_armies", "p_conquer")] })) head(even, 10) #> # A tibble: 10 × 3 #>    def_armies att_armies p_conquer #>         <int>      <int>     <dbl> #>  1          1          3     0.754 #>  2          2          4     0.656 #>  3          3          5     0.642 #>  4          4          6     0.638 #>  5          5          6     0.506 #>  6          6          7     0.521 #>  7          7          8     0.536 #>  8          8          9     0.547 #>  9          9         10     0.558 #> 10         10         11     0.568 rk_plot_odds_heatmap(att_range = 2:20, def_range = 1:20)

title: The probability of Risk
text: Exact odds settle game, game sequence decisions battles fight. built-agents encode three answers: "random" attacks random, "aggressive" attacks weakest reachable enemy outnumbers , "cautious" attacks army ratio otherwise consolidates. rk_tournament() deals fresh board every game plays .  Win rates depend round cap: aggression rewarded games cut short, patience allowed run.
code: results <- rk_tournament(   c(Red = "aggressive", Blue = "cautious", Green = "random"),   n_games = 12,   max_rounds = 40,   seed = 1 ) results #> # A tibble: 3 × 7 #>   player strategy   games  wins win_rate mean_territories mean_rounds #>   <chr>  <chr>      <int> <int>    <dbl>            <dbl>       <dbl> #> 1 Red    aggressive    12     5    0.417             17.5        18.2 #> 2 Blue   cautious      12     3    0.25              10.5        18.2 #> 3 Green  random        12     4    0.333             14          18.2 rk_plot_tournament(results) caps <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(10, 40), function(cap) {   out <- rk_tournament(     c(Red = "aggressive", Blue = "cautious"),     n_games = 8, max_rounds = cap, seed = 2   )   out$max_rounds <- cap   out })) caps[, c("max_rounds", "player", "strategy", "win_rate", "mean_rounds")] #> # A tibble: 4 × 5 #>   max_rounds player strategy   win_rate mean_rounds #>        <dbl> <chr>  <chr>         <dbl>       <dbl> #> 1         10 Red    aggressive     0.25        8    #> 2         10 Blue   cautious       0.5         8    #> 3         40 Red    aggressive     0.75        8.38 #> 4         40 Blue   cautious       0.25        8.38

text: supplied strategies : "random" Spreads reinforcements random, picks uniformly among legal attacks, ending turn probability 0.25 decision point. "aggressive" Stacks every reinforcement strongest frontier territory attacks weakest reachable enemy long outnumbers defender. "cautious" Reinforces weakest frontier, attacks attacking armies least ratio times defending armies, otherwise pulls armies interior towards frontier.

title: Built-in artificial-intelligence agents — rk_ai
code: bot <- rk_ai("aggressive") game <- rk_game(c("Red", "Blue"), seed = 1) bot(game, "Red")$action #> [1] "reinforce"

title: Expected losses and win probability for a single dice duel — rk_duel_odds
text: one-row tibble::tibble() columns: n_att integer, attacker dice. n_def integer, defender dice. e_att_loss double, expected armies lost attacker. e_def_loss double, expected armies lost defender, equal min(n_att, n_def) - e_att_loss. sd_loss double, standard deviation attacker's loss. p_att_wins_all double, probability attacker wins every compared pair, .e. att_loss == 0. p_def_wins_all double, probability defender wins every compared pair, .e. att_loss == min(n_att, n_def). p_split double, probability sides lose exactly one army. split needs two compared pairs, 0 whenever one pair compared – case p_att_wins_all + p_def_wins_all equals 1.
